title: Going beyond RAG: Extended Mind Transformers - Phoebe Klett
talk_summary: Phoebe Klett presents Extended Mind Transformers, a modification to the attention mechanism that stores key-value representations of memory tokens and lets query tokens retrieve them by cosine similarity during generation, avoiding fine-tuning and long-context stuffing. She shows competitive retrieval performance up to 16k tokens, token-level causal citations, and uncertainty-triggered re-generation with more retrieved memories.

takeaways.what_they_do: Uses token-level entropy over the output distribution to detect uncertain tokens, then regenerates those steps with more retrieved memory tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we kind of can detect that the model is uncertain about that token we can regenerate that step using more information from these memories

takeaways.what_they_do: Retrieves many candidate memory tokens but discards those below a cosine similarity threshold (e.g., 0.25) before attending, to avoid confusing the model with irrelevant matches.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if they're not at least like 0.25 similar then we'll just throw them out

takeaways.what_they_do: Eliminates tokens corresponding to unknown tokens from the memory before retrieval because they match queries spuriously without carrying useful information.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just eliminate those from the memory before we allow it to start retrieving

takeaways.what_they_do: Because retrieval happens inside attention, the model can report exactly which memory tokens were attended to when generating each output token, giving causal rather than post-hoc citations.
